profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the lead for a global surgery qualitative research workstream and the implementation coordinator for partner-site engagement, focused on aligning interfaces for a multi-country project that will synthesize interviews and operational notes into a practical framework for improving international surgical teaching collaborations (ISTCs). Context: the team has completed most interviews across three partner regions and now needs to coordinate the handoff between coding, site validation, and production of a shared framework brief for external collaborators. Agenda: confirm what counts as the current master framework draft, align on what materials will be sent to partner hospitals for 'validation,' clarify who updates the shared evidence tracker, and make sure the end-of-month package is 'ready to share.' Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned the handoff between analysis and partner engagement, the validation packet content, ownership of the tracker, and the status of the framework brief.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Qualitative health systems research, interview coding, framework synthesis, global surgery collaboration studies
members.background: A public health researcher based at a university global surgery center who has led multi-country qualitative studies and usually works with coded transcripts, analytic memos, and manuscript-oriented synthesis processes.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the analytic framing stable long enough to finish a credible cross-site synthesis and avoid partner feedback reopening category structure before the evidence table is mature.
hidden_assumptions: The 'framework draft' means the analytic version in the shared drive that reflects the latest coded themes, even if the visual formatting is unfinished.
Site 'validation' means checking whether the synthesized themes feel recognizable and non-misleading, not reopening wording line by line or requesting missing operational details.
The evidence tracker is owned by the analysis team once interviews are coded, and partner-engagement staff mainly consume it rather than edit it directly.
If something is 'ready to share' by month-end, it can be circulated internally to core institutional partners as a near-final draft without publication-grade formatting.

members.name: Samuel Okoro
members.expertise: Cross-institutional program coordination, partner communications, surgical education operations, stakeholder feedback workflows
members.background: A program manager who has supported teaching partnerships between academic hospitals and regional training sites, and who typically works through partner review cycles, action trackers, and implementation-facing briefing packs.
members.private_state: He wants partner hospitals to feel visibly included before the framework is finalized and is trying to avoid sending anything that looks academically provisional or difficult for non-research collaborators to act on.
hidden_assumptions: The 'framework draft' means the partner-facing slide version that groups findings into practical collaboration domains with examples and suggested actions.
Site 'validation' means partner representatives review the framework for completeness, flag omissions, and suggest revisions before it is treated as settled.
The evidence tracker is a live shared artifact across workstreams, so whoever learns of a site-specific correction or clarification should update it directly.
If something is 'ready to share' by month-end, it should be polished enough to send to external hospital partners without caveats about formatting or remaining synthesis work.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the current framework draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the framework draft' as if it is one shared object.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the versioned analytic matrix and narrative draft in the research drive, labeled v0.8, which still has dense theme language and placeholder layout.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the partner-facing slide deck outline assembled from earlier summaries, labeled April partner deck, which is shorter and organized around actionable domains.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts have been casually called 'the framework draft' in prior emails, and each participant assumes the other naturally means the document most relevant to their own workstream.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that partner sites should do a 'validation pass.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks validation is a credibility check on whether the synthesized themes resonate with site experience, mainly through high-level comments from a small number of representatives.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks validation is a substantive review round in which sites can correct framing, add context, and reshape the framework before circulation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Validation is a standard, respectable term in both research and implementation settings, so mutual agreement sounds natural even though each side imports a different level of revision authority.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership of the shared evidence tracker
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'keep the tracker updated' after partner conversations.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes Samuel will send notes or flagged issues to the analysis team, which will decide what enters the tracker to preserve coding consistency and version control.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes he and regional coordinators can directly edit the live tracker as they receive partner clarifications, since it is the operational hub for all workstreams.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both endorse the same goal of having an updated tracker, and shared cloud tools make direct editing feel obvious to coordinators while governance boundaries feel obvious to researchers.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'ready to share' means at month-end
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on making the package 'ready to share' by the end of the month.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means the synthesis packet is sufficiently stable for internal circulation among core project institutions, with citations, evidence links, and caveats still intact.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means the package is clean, concise, and polished enough for external dissemination to partner hospitals and teaching leads.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are oriented toward timely coordination and use the same deadline language, but neither thinks to specify audience or finish-level because 'share' sounds self-explanatory in their own workflow.

turns.inner_thought: I want to get the handoff contained before this turns into another open-ended partner revision cycle. The analytic matrix in the shared research drive is almost stable enough to circulate internally, and I need that to remain the anchor. If we can agree that the framework draft moves into a light validation pass and then to something ready to share by month-end, we can protect the synthesis from being reopened too early.

turns.inner_thought: Good, this is the moment to make sure Maya knows partners are expecting a usable product, not a researcher-facing work file. The partner-facing slide deck is what sites will understand, and they need to see it soon if they are going to do a meaningful validation pass before we send anything out more broadly at the end of the month.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. From the outreach side, the sites are already expecting to see the framework draft fairly soon, and they are keen to do a validation pass before the end of the month.

turns.utterance: That timing should be workable. The framework draft is nearly there now that Kenya and Rwanda are fully integrated; I just need to fold the final Uganda memo into the matrix.

turns.inner_thought: I should set a boundary here without sounding rigid. turns.utterance: Just so we're calibrated, for validation I mainly want partners to confirm that the themes feel recognizable and to flag anything clearly off, rather than getting into extensive reworking at this stage.

turns.utterance: Yes, exactly. And I think the sites will appreciate having a bit of room to fill gaps and refine the examples so the framework is stronger before it's shared more broadly.

turns.inner_thought: Now the tracker. I need him to funnel comments back in a controlled way. If I say 'keep the tracker updated,' he should understand that partner feedback gets logged and then incorporated through our normal synthesis checks.
turns.utterance: On the workflow side, as partner comments come in, we should keep the tracker updated so the evidence table stays aligned with the coded material.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect, so we are treating the tracker as the live shared hub. I'll have the regional coordinators and me enter clarifications directly after each call while details are fresh. That will help everyone see the latest picture without waiting on another handoff.
turns.utterance: Agreed. I can make sure the regional coordinators and I update the tracker directly right after each validation call so those clarifications are captured while they're fresh.

turns.inner_thought: Good, as long as comments are in there for us to review, my team can lock language. That's enough to call it ready to share from a research workstream perspective.
turns.utterance: That's helpful. Once those updates are in, my team can lock the framework language and make the package ready to share by month-end.

turns.inner_thought: Excellent, then we should be on track for external circulation. If it's ready to share by month-end, I can send the polished version to hospital education leads ahead of the early-June partnership calls. That's exactly the timing I needed.
